title: Greetings and introducing yourself
goal: By the end of this lesson you can greet people formally and casually, introduce yourself (name, origin, where you live), say goodbye, and handle the Montreal 'Bonjour-hi' at the counter.

body: *Bonjour* (good day) is the all-purpose greeting, polite with everyone, from morning to late afternoon. *Bonsoir* (good evening) is used from around supper time on.
*Salut* (hi) is casual: friends, coworkers, people your age. In Quebec, *Allô!* is also a friendly 'hi' face to face, not only on the phone.
learn.tip: Always start with Bonjour when you walk into a shop or office. Skipping it sounds rude.

body: Casual: *Ça va?* (How's it going?) — answer *Ça va bien* (good), *Ça va* (OK), *Pas pire* (not bad, very Quebec). Polite: *Comment allez-vous?* — answer *Je vais bien, merci. Et vous?*
With a friend: *Comment ça va?* or *Comment vas-tu?* — answer *Bien, et toi?*

head: Question
Answer
rows: Oui, ça va bien. Et toi?

body: Give your name with *Je m'appelle…* (or casually *Moi, c'est…*). Say where you come from with *Je viens de…* or *Je suis de…*, and where you live with *J'habite à…*.
When you meet someone: *Enchanté* (a man says it) / *Enchantée* (a woman writes it; same sound). In Quebec you will also hear *Content de te rencontrer* or simply *Allô, ça va?*

*Au revoir* is the neutral goodbye. *Bonne journée!* (have a good day) and *Bonne soirée!* (have a good evening) are what you hear at every counter. *À demain* = see you tomorrow, *À plus tard* or *À plus* = see you later, *À la prochaine* = until next time.

In Quebec, *Bye!* or *Bye-bye!* is very common in casual French, and *À tantôt* means 'see you later today'. After *merci*, Quebecers often answer *Bienvenue!* (you're welcome) as well as the standard *De rien* or *Avec plaisir*.
learn.tip: Quebec 'tantôt' = later today or earlier today, depending on the verb tense.

body: In many downtown Montreal stores, staff greet you with *Bonjour-hi!* to let you choose the language. Your answer decides the language of the conversation: answer *Bonjour!* and they will continue in French.
Elsewhere in Quebec, you'll just hear *Bonjour!* — and in casual places, *Allô!* or *Salut!*

quebec.intro: Quebec greetings are warm and quick: Salut, ça va?, Allô!, Pas pire, Bienvenue. In downtown Montreal stores, 'Bonjour-hi' invites you to pick the language: answer in French.

items.note: informal; pas pire is positive in Quebec
very common in Quebec; avoid it in France, where it only means 'welcome'
tantôt also exists in France but is far more common in Quebec
downtown Montreal stores; answer Bonjour! to continue in French

dialogue.fr: Ça va bien, merci. Un café, s'il vous plaît.
dialogue.en: I'm good, thanks. A coffee, please.

dialogue.fr: Voilà. Vous êtes nouveau dans le quartier?
dialogue.en: Here you go. Are you new in the neighbourhood?

dialogue.en: Yes, I come from Toronto. My name is Ryan.
Nice to meet you, Ryan! I'm Karim.
Thanks, Karim! Have a good day!

speak.prompt: Introduce yourself in 3 sentences: name, where you come from, where you live.
speak.model: Bonjour! Je m'appelle Ryan. Je viens de Toronto. J'habite à Montréal.

speak.prompt: Greet a friend casually and answer 'Ça va?' the Quebec way.
speak.model: Salut! Ça va? — Pas pire, toi?

speak.prompt: A cashier says 'Bonjour-hi!'. Answer, order a coffee, and say goodbye.
speak.model: Bonjour! Un café, s'il vous plaît. Merci, bonne journée!

write.prompt: Write a short message (4–6 sentences) introducing yourself to a new French-speaking neighbour.
write.model: Bonjour! Je m'appelle Ryan. Je viens de Toronto, mais j'habite à Montréal maintenant. J'habite au numéro 12. Je parle un peu français. Bonne journée!

quiz.why: Salut is for friends and casual settings.
It uses vous: polite or plural.
Quebecers use allô as a friendly hello in person.
tantôt = a bit later (or earlier) today.

quiz.q: Which is the standard goodbye at a store counter?
What does 'Pas pire' mean in Quebec?
